title: Can Pet Urine Stains Be Sanded Out of Hardwood Floors? Honest Answers From Everett Jobs
meta: Light pet urine stains sand out; black ones usually do not. Wills Flooring shares what really happens on Everett refinish jobs, with prices and options.
keywords: pet urine stains hardwood floors sanding, can dog urine stains be sanded out, black pet stains hardwood floor refinish, Everett hardwood floor refinishing pet stains, remove dog pee stains from wood floors

blocks.lead: Yellow and light brown pet stains usually sand out. Black or gray-black stains usually do not, because the urine has reacted with the wood itself, not just the finish.
blocks.detail: On Everett jobs we get roughly two out of three pet-stained floors looking clean with sanding alone. The rest need bleaching, board replacement or a dark stain to hide what is left. We tell you which before we quote.

blocks.html: This is the question we get most from Everett landlords turning over a Silver Lake rental and from buyers who just pulled up the carpet in a Riverside bungalow and found a constellation of dark spots. The honest answer depends on how deep the urine went, and nobody can tell you that from a photo. Here is how we judge it on site, what sanding actually removes, and what your options are when it does not.

blocks.text: What urine actually does to a hardwood floor

items.title: Sits on the finish
items.text: A fresh accident wiped up within hours leaves at most a dull patch in the finish. On a floor with an intact polyurethane coat this is a screen-and-recoat problem at $1.99 per sq ft, not a sanding problem at all.

items.title: Soaks into the top of the wood
items.text: Repeated accidents or one that sat overnight get through the finish and into the top 1/32 in of the board. The wood turns yellow or light brown. This is what a full sand removes. Most Everett floors with a single-dog history sit here.

items.title: Reacts with tannins
items.text: Urine is ammonia-rich and alkaline. Given weeks or months, it reacts with the tannins in oak and turns the wood fibers black, often 1/8 in deep or more. Sanding that deep would take the floor below its safe thickness. This is the black stain everyone worries about.

items.title: Reaches the subfloor
items.text: Years of a litter box or an old dog in one corner and the urine is in the plywood underneath. The boards can be replaced, but the odor lives below. In Everett crawlspace homes it can come up through the joists on warm days.

blocks.text: Your options when the black stain will not sand out

items.html: Two-part wood bleach. A peroxide-based bleach applied after sanding lightens dark stains by a shade or two. It rarely makes them vanish, and it lightens the surrounding oak too, so it works best when the whole floor is going light or getting a stain afterward.

Stain the floor darker. A medium to dark stain at $6.50 per sq ft hides most brown ghosts and softens black ones. It does not hide raised or punky grain. This is the most common answer on Everett resale flips because it also modernizes the floor.

Replace the boards. We cut out the stained boards, weave in new oak of the same width, and sand everything together. On a natural finish the patch is nearly invisible after six months of sun. Priced per board on site.
Replace the floor. Only when the subfloor is saturated or the boards are too thin to sand again. See our post on refinish or replace for how we make that call.

blocks.title: The odor test nobody does:
blocks.text: Before we sand, we mist the stain with water and smell it. Wet wood releases old ammonia. If the smell comes back strong, the urine is below the boards and sanding alone will not fix it, no matter how clean the top looks. Ask any refinisher in Everett to do this before they quote you.
Sanding out stains vs replacing boards

a.title: Enough when
items: Stains are yellow to light brown

You are open to a stain color if a ghost remains

b.title: Needed when
items: Stains are black or the grain is raised
Odor returns on humid Everett days
The floor has already been sanded three or more times
You want a natural finish with no color to hide behind

blocks.text: How to get a straight answer on pet stains

items.html: Ask for a test sand on the worst spot. It takes five minutes with a hand sander and tells you more than any photo. We do it during the free estimate.
Get the fallback priced up front. Your quote should say what happens if a stain stays: bleach, stain color or board swap, with a per-board price.
Add dust containment if the pet still lives there. $250 keeps ammonia-laden sanding dust out of the rest of the house, which matters in occupied Everett homes.
Fix the cause first. Old dog, new medication, litter box location. A refinish on a floor that is still being used as a bathroom is money down the drain.
Check who is doing the finish. Wills Flooring are Bona Certified Craftsmen with a 1-year workmanship warranty, and our refinishing page lists exactly what the $3.99 rate includes.

faq.q: Can black dog urine stains be sanded out of hardwood?
faq.a: Usually not. Black stains mean the urine has reacted with tannins in the oak and discolored the wood fibers, often deeper than a safe sanding can reach. The realistic fixes are two-part wood bleach, a darker stain to hide the ghost, or cutting out and replacing the affected boards.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish pet-stained hardwood floors in Everett?
faq.a: The refinish itself is the same as any floor: $3.99 per sq ft natural or $6.50 with stain at Wills Flooring, 500 sq ft minimum. Board replacement and bleaching are extras priced per spot at the free estimate once we have test-sanded the worst stain.

faq.q: Will refinishing get rid of the pet urine smell?
faq.a: If the urine stayed in the top of the boards, yes, sanding removes the affected wood and the new finish seals it. If the smell comes back when you mist the spot with water, the urine is in the subfloor, and only replacing the boards and sealing or replacing the subfloor below will fix it.

faq.q: Does hydrogen peroxide remove urine stains from hardwood floors?
faq.a: Drugstore peroxide lightens fresh, shallow stains slightly and can blotch the finish around them. Professional two-part wood bleach applied to bare sanded wood works better on brown stains but rarely erases black ones, and it lightens the surrounding oak, so it belongs in a full refinish, not a spot fix.

faq.q: Can I just replace the stained boards without refinishing the whole floor?
faq.a: You can, but the new boards will not match the old finish, and a spot sand almost always shows. The clean approach is to weave in new boards and then sand and finish the whole room so everything ages together. Many Everett customers combine this with a rental turnover.

faq.q: Is it better to stain the floor dark to hide pet stains?
faq.a: It is the cheapest way to hide light and medium ghosts, and a medium brown on red oak looks current in Everett homes. It will not hide black stains with raised grain, and dark floors show dust and dog hair more. We usually suggest a medium tone rather than espresso.
